## The bottleneck distance

For diagrams $D_1, D_2$, the bottleneck distance is
$$
d_B(D_1, D_2) = \inf_{\gamma} \sup_{x \in D_1} \lVert x - \gamma(x) \rVert_\infty,
$$
where $\gamma$ ranges over bijections between the diagrams (points may be matched to the diagonal).

## The stability theorem

For tame functions $f, g$ on a triangulable space (Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner and Harer, 2007):
$$
d_B\big(\mathrm{Dgm}(f), \mathrm{Dgm}(g)\big) \le \lVert f - g \rVert_\infty.
$$

✏️ *Explain what this means for noisy data, and mention Wasserstein distances.*
